en: For many tasks, AI models need to find
information.
And if you're working with a large language
model in an AI agent, it may search for
information by performing web search, if a
respective tool exists, by searching your
file system, maybe by connecting to a vector
database and performing RAG,
or in other ways. And the part where it
searches your file system, that is also
called agentic search, which is another
important term. The idea simply is that if
you give an AI agent access to your file
system, potentially in a sandbox, then the
large language model can make decisions on
which files to take a closer look at. And
that turns out to be quite efficient because
these large language models turn out to make
quite good decisions when it comes to
identifying identifying the files that look
promising and requesting those files to be
read.
So whenever you hear the term agentic
search, it's simply about giving an AI model
the tools or allowing it to request the use
of tools that allow it to search the hard
drive on your behalf. Because of course, as
a human, if you're looking for information,
you also may be scanning a file system. You
may be looking at files, trying to figure
out which files sound like they may contain
the information. You're looking for
and opening some of these files to take a
look.
You as a human, you are quite slow at that.
The computer, of course, is much faster, and
that's exactly why AI agents are pretty good
at agentic search. They can search for
information in a file system at quite a high
speed. And that's the concept behind agentic
search, AI-powered search through your file
system looking for certain information or a
certain file.
